licenses.text:
Douay-Rheims 1899, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/engdrv/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "Douay-Rheims 1899
The Holy Bible in English, Douay-Rheims American Edition of 1899, translated from the Latin Vulgate
Public Domain
Language: English
Dialect: archaic American
Translation by: English College, Douai

This Public Domain Bible text is brought to you courtesy of eBible.org.
Help support free Bible access at https://eBible.org/give.php."

Why this is public domain:
The Douay-Rheims translation was first published in 1582 (New Testament) and 1609-1610 (Old Testament) in France for English Catholics; the American Edition of 1899, published in the United States, is the text used. Everyone who made the translation and its revision died more than 70 years ago, so it is public domain in the United States (its country of origin here, and published before 1931) and in the United Kingdom.

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page
(https://ebible.org/details.php?id=engdrv) and the edition's own files.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-engdrv-413fc29d, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
